title: The subjunctive mood
keyIdea: The subjunctive is a special verb form used in very formal writing and speech. For something imagined or wished, it uses were for every subject: If I were you; I wish she were here. After words that ask for something to happen, such as insist, suggest, recommend, demand, vital and essential, it uses the base form of the verb for every subject: The coach insists that he be on time; I suggest that Sam check his work. Very formal writing can also drop if and put were first: Were they to arrive early, we would start. A plain past fact still uses was: When I was five.
familyTip: Play "If I were…" at the table: each person finishes If I were an animal, I would… Then try a bossy one: I insist that everyone ___ their plate (clear, not clears). Point out that If I was you is fine when chatting, but a formal letter or speech uses If I were you.

visual.caption: Formal subjunctive, or everyday English? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: If I were taller, I could reach.
If I was taller, I could reach.
We ask that she be quiet.
We ask her to be quiet.
Were it to snow, school would close.
It is essential that he arrive early.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: was or were, find the trigger word and pick the base form, build Were they to…, spot subjunctives in a letter, sort formal from everyday.

kid: Some verbs change when we talk about things that are not real. If I were a bird, I would fly. I am not a bird. It is made up, so we say were, not was.
We use were for wishes too. I wish it were Friday. It is not Friday yet. But for a real thing, keep was: When I was five, I lived by the sea.
Some words ask for something to happen: insist, suggest, demand. After them, use the plain verb. The coach insists that he be on time. I suggest that Sam check his work. No s, and be, not is.
This is how people talk in a speech or a letter to the head. With friends, If I was you is fine. In formal writing, use If I were you.
adult: Ages 10 to 11. In England this is Year 6 grammar. Pupils learn the difference between informal and formal structures, including subjunctive forms such as If I were or Were they to come in very formal writing and speech. The National Curriculum glossary gives The school requires that all pupils be honest as an example.

English has two common subjunctive forms. The were-subjunctive marks something unreal or wished. It uses were for every subject: If I were you; I wish she were here; as if he were king. The base-form subjunctive follows words that demand, suggest or need something (insist, suggest, recommend, require, demand, essential, vital): that he be ready, that she attend, that pupils not run. There is no -s ending, be takes the place of is and are, and not goes straight before the verb.

Formal writing can also invert a condition: If they were to arrive early becomes Were they to arrive early, and if drops out. In everyday speech, was and an -s ending are normal (If I was you; I suggest he goes), so these are register choices, not errors in chat.

Common mistakes: treating every were as a subjunctive (Pupils were late is a plain past); using were for a real past event (If he was late this morning, he missed the register is right); adding -s or will after insist that; writing doesn't instead of not; and keeping if when inverting (If were they to come). In the lab your child fills five gaps, fixes four demands, builds three inversions, finds three subjunctives in a letter and sorts six cards.

practice.prompt: Formal writing: "If I ___ the teacher, I would give less homework."
practice.hint: Are you the teacher, or is it imagined?
practice.explain: It is imagined, so formal writing uses were, even with I. Was is fine in chat.

practice.prompt: A formal letter has {n} sentences that start "It is vital that…". Each one needs one base-form verb. How many base-form verbs is that?
practice.hint: One base-form verb follows each "vital that".
practice.explain: Each of the {n} sentences takes one base-form verb, such as bring or be, so {n} in all.

choices: I suggest that she go home.
I suggest that she goes home.
I suggest that she went home.
practice.hint: After suggest that, use the plain verb with no ending.
practice.explain: Go is the base form. Goes has -s, and went is past.

practice.prompt: A speech has {a} "If I were…" lines and {b} "I wish it were…" lines. How many times is were used?
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} uses of were, each for something imagined or wished.

choices: Were they to call, I would answer.
practice.hint: Which one means "if they were to…"?
practice.explain: Were they to call means if they were to call, an imagined event. They were at the park is a plain past fact.

pool.prompt: Formal: "The rules require that every pupil ___ a hat."
pool.hint: After require that, use the base form.
pool.explain: Wear is the base form, the same for every subject. Wears adds -s, and will is not needed.

pool.prompt: "When I ___ seven, I learned to swim." Which verb?
pool.hint: Did this really happen, or is it imagined?
pool.explain: It is a real past fact, so was. Were is for imagined or wished things.

pool.prompt: Which is the formal version of "If she were to win, she would share the prize"?
choices: Were she to win, she would share the prize.
If were she to win, she would share the prize.
She were to win, she would share the prize.
pool.hint: Were goes first, and if drops out.
pool.explain: Were moves in front of the subject and does the job of if.

pool.prompt: Formal: "It is essential that he ___ ready by nine."
pool.hint: Essential asks for something to happen.
pool.explain: After essential that, the base form be is used for every subject.

pool.prompt: Which word is a trigger for the base-form subjunctive?
pool.hint: Which word asks for something to happen?
pool.explain: Recommend asks for an action: I recommend that she attend. Remember and notice report facts.

pool.prompt: In a letter, {n} sentences use "that he be". How many of them use "is"?
pool.hint: In the subjunctive, be replaces is.
pool.explain: The subjunctive uses be, so 0 of the {n} sentences use is.

pool.prompt: Formal: "The head asks that pupils ___ run in the hall."
pool.hint: In the subjunctive, not goes straight before the verb.
pool.explain: That pupils not run: no do, just not and the base form.

pool.prompt: Where would you most expect "If I were you"?
choices: A quick text to a friend
pool.hint: The subjunctive is a formal choice.
pool.explain: The subjunctive belongs in formal writing and speech. In a text to a friend, If I was you is normal.

pool.prompt: A class writes {n} formal sentences that start "I wish it…". All are about things that are not true now. How many use were?
pool.hint: A wish about now is imagined.
pool.explain: Every one is a wish, so all {n} use were in formal writing.
